hadith:
Patients - Narrated Sa`d:

Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to visit me during my ailment which had been aggravated during Hajjat-al- Wada`. I said to him, "You see how sick I am. I have much property but have no heir except my only daughter May I give two thirds of my property in charity?"! He said, "No." I said, "Half of it?" He said, "No." I said "One third?" He said, "One third is too much, for to leave your heirs rich is better than to leave them poor, begging of others. Nothing you spend seeking Allah's pleasure but you shall get a reward for it, even for what you put in the mouth of your wife."
message: When hardship strikes, turn to Allah with sincere devotion as mentioned in Surah Luqman, for He alone can deliver us from our trials. Remember that gratitude for His blessings and spending in His way—even the smallest act—brings immense reward, and trust in Al Hakam, the Judge, knowing He alone determines what is truly just and fair for us in this life and the Hereafter.
name:
Al Hakam - الْحَكَمُ - The Judge

The name Al Hakam emphasizes Allah's role as the supreme judge who determines justice and fairness. It signifies His authority to rule over His creation and to decide matters, rewarding the righteous and punishing the wrongdoers. The use of this name serves to remind believers of the ultimate accountability they have in the Hereafter.
verse:
Luqman - Luqman - 31:32

And as soon as they are overwhelmed by waves like mountains, they cry out to Allah ˹alone˺ in sincere devotion. But when He delivers them ˹safely˺ to shore, only some become relatively grateful. And none rejects Our signs except whoever is deceitful, ungrateful.
